items.item: Recursive Hilbert-ball coloring of dyadic partitions, driven by a fixed-point-free Lipschitz map
items.pivot_distance: about 2 from L (estimated; no trace)
items.for: Highest item confidence in the pass. Six earlier claimed proofs (Shavgulidze, Akhmedov ×2, Beklaryan, Moore 2012, Wajnryb–Witowicz) never used vector-valued or recursive invariants. A one-line definition turns a 50-year-old problem into about two pages: the Cook–Reckhow profile.
items.against: Unrefereed (the Lean now compiles and passes Comparator, 2026-10-10). The definition's own reach is narrow: groups that contain F get nonamenability from the theorem, not from the device. The fixed-point-free map itself is transfer (Benyamini–Sternfeld).
items.next_test: Rerun the device on n-adic cells for F_n without F's transports, then on Stein F_{2,3} and F_τ; compare with and without the colouring in the library.
items.verdict: The closest match in the corpus to the extension-variable profile. The colour p(T) is a defined object that is absent from the statement and exists only to drive the proof. It dissolves a real obstruction: Følner sets control only averages of bounded functions, while the natural invariant (depth) is unbounded, so the proof needs a bounded invariant that never stabilises. Its ingredient, the Benyamini–Sternfeld map, is transfer (N0). The coupling to F's self-similarity has no precedent found, and six earlier claimed proofs never used a vector-valued recursive invariant, so it looks hard to construct. Two things stand between this and a confirmed jump. (a) The proof is unrefereed; the Lean now compiles and passes Comparator (2026-10-10), so the formal theorem is certified, though the device must still be confirmed to be the one the formal proof uses. (b) The strict definition needs speedups on OTHER theorems, and the definition's own reach looks narrow: groups that contain F inherit nonamenability from the theorem, not from the device, so they test nothing. It may be a one-problem key rather than a jump.

f1_review.verdict: The closest match in the corpus to the extension-variable profile. The colour p(T) is a defined object that is absent from the statement and exists only to drive the proof. It dissolves a real obstruction: Følner sets control only averages of bounded functions, while the natural invariant (depth) is unbounded, so the proof needs a bounded invariant that never stabilises. Its ingredient, the Benyamini–Sternfeld map, is transfer (N0). The coupling to F's self-similarity has no precedent found, and six earlier claimed proofs never used a vector-valued recursive invariant, so it looks hard to construct. Two things stand between this and a confirmed jump. (a) The proof is unrefereed and the Lean has not been built; if the proof is wrong the item is void. (b) The strict definition needs speedups on OTHER theorems, and the definition's own reach looks narrow: groups that contain F inherit nonamenability from the theorem, not from the device, so they test nothing. It may be a one-problem key rather than a jump. [Update 2026-10-10: the 248 Lean now compiles and passes Comparator; see data/lean_checks.json.]
f1_review.decisive_test: Re-run the device directly on Farey or n-adic cells for Monod's H(A) and Lodha–Moore G_0, without embedding F, and derive an explicit Kesten-norm bound for F. Negative controls must fail: the amenable IET subgroups and family 253's polygon-exchange group.

f1_review.grade: N3 provisional (novelty conf 0.35), F1; likely N2
f1_review.verdict: F1-shaped: it adjoins a new auxiliary variable, like an extension variable. Under the strict rule, though, the mechanism is mostly transfer. Stochastic localization with the I-MMSE chain rule, Tao's entropy decrement and Russo–Zou information budgets already say 'pay for many adaptively chosen statistics with one information budget'. The new part is the instantiation in Fourier analysis: ferromagnetic thermal noise makes character decoding exact and independent of the number of frequencies. That reads as a new bridge (N2) unless the speedup test shows it does something those templates cannot. (An earlier Lean caveat is retracted: the fixed ε_j is exactly the instance the paper uses, and the label is on the chain to the comparator.) It has the lowest prior here but the highest value of information, because its downstream test is concrete and would be decisive.

f1_review.verdict: The object is literally the Borcea–Brändén symbol of the permutation operator, so it is N0. What is new is a bridge: contracting the symbol over unpinned layer points produces Tóth's cycle weight 2, so BBL negative dependence carries over from θ = 1 to θ = 2. That is the separate Tier 3 'splice' item, F5 and not F1, and all of its reuse is inside family 271. The downstream agent also finds the splice's mechanism in Asano (1970) and Suzuki–Fisher (1971), so the splice is likely N2 too (moved to Tier 4).

f1_review.item: Character classes z_i(t) (Hilbert–Smith in every dimension)
f1_review.verdict: This is a profinite, germ-localised version of the classical isotypic G-signature divisibility (Hirzebruch–Zagier, Atiyah–Singer, Izumi's Rokhlin K-theory). Every component has precedent; only the combination and the lift through an odd-degree localization are new. If the proof is correct the theorem is enormous, but its downstream reach (weak Hilbert–Smith, Lie-hypothesis removals) comes through corollaries of the theorem, not reuse of the device, so it does not count toward a jump.
f1_review.decisive_test: Port the device to ENR Z-homology manifolds (generalised Hilbert–Smith). That is the only target where the device itself does new work. It would rise to N3 only if the finite-group template fails there without the new localization step.
